questions.question: Which of the following statements about the second five-year plan is INCORRECT?

options.text: The plan stressed the rapid industrialisation of heavy and basic industries.
Electricity, Railway, Steel etc. industries were established during the plan.
The plan was based on the Keynesian Model.
The socialist pattern of the society was reflected in the plan.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The plan was based on the Keynesian Model**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961) focused on the rapid industrialization of heavy and basic industries.
 
• During this plan, industries such as electricity, railways, and steel were significantly developed.
 
• The plan was based on the Mahalanobis Model, not the Keynesian Model.
 
• The plan aimed to establish a socialist pattern of society in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961)**

 
 
• The Second Five-Year Plan was launched under the leadership of Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• This plan was designed to build a strong industrial base for India, focusing on heavy industries and public sector enterprises.
 
• The Mahalanobis Model, formulated by Indian statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis, was used as the basis for this plan. It emphasized the importance of investment in heavy industries and aimed at achieving self-reliance in industrial production.
 
• The plan also sought to reduce inequalities in income and wealth and aimed to move towards a more equitable and socialist society.
 
 
 
• **Keynesian Model**
 
 
• The Keynesian Model, developed by John Maynard Keynes, focuses on total spending in the economy and its effects on output and inflation.
 
• Keynesian economics advocates for increased government expenditures and lower taxes to stimulate demand and pull an economy out of depression.
 
• It is often used to justify government intervention in the economy, especially during recessions.
 
• This model is more focused on addressing short-term economic fluctuations rather than long-term industrial planning.
 
 
 
• **Socialist Pattern of Society**
 
 
• The concept of a socialist pattern of society aims at reducing inequalities in income and wealth and providing equal opportunities for all citizens.
 
• It involves the establishment of a mixed economy where both the public and private sectors coexist and contribute to economic development.
 
• In the context of India, this meant a significant role for the public sector in key industries and infrastructure, while also allowing space for private enterprise.
 
• This approach was intended to ensure that economic growth would benefit all sections of society and lead to a more equitable distribution of resources.

• **Kharif Crops**

 
 
• Kharif crops, also known as monsoon crops, are sown with the beginning of the first rains in July, during the southwest monsoon season.
 
• They require a lot of water and hot weather for their growth.
 
• Examples of kharif crops include **Paddy, Soyabean, Maize, Cotton, and Groundnut**.

• **Difference Between Kharif and Rabi Crops**
 
 
• The main difference lies in the timing of their sowing and harvesting seasons.
 
• Kharif crops are dependent on the arrival of the monsoon, whereas rabi crops are grown in the winter season when the monsoon has retreated.
 
• Kharif crops need a lot of water and hot weather, while rabi crops require cold weather for growth and less water.
 
 
 
• **Important Indian Cropping Seasons**
 
 
• India has two main cropping seasons - Rabi and Kharif, and a third, less significant one called Zaid.
 
• Zaid crops are grown between March and June, in the intervening period between the rabi and kharif seasons.

• They have the power to hear appeals and to issue writs to enforce Fundamental Rights.
 
• The judges of the High Courts are appointed by the President of India.
 
 
 
• **District Courts**
 
 
• District Courts are established by the state governments of India for every district or for one or more districts together taking into account the number of cases and population distribution.
 
• They administer justice at the district level and are subordinate to the High Court of the respective state.
 
 
 
• **Subordinate Courts**
 
 
• Subordinate Courts are the lower courts under the District Courts, which deal with civil, criminal, and other cases at a more local level.
 
• They operate under the supervision and control of the District Court.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court**

• It comprises the Chief Justice of India and a number of other judges appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Supreme Court has extensive original, appellate, and advisory jurisdictions.

questions.question: Who first stated the principle of refraction that postulates that every substance has a specific bending ratio – 'refractive index'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Willebrord Snellius**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Willebrord Snellius** was a Dutch astronomer and mathematician.
 
• He is best known for the law of refraction of light, now known as **Snell's Law**.
 
• Snell's Law describes how light bends, or refracts, when it passes from one transparent medium to another.
 
• He formulated this principle in 1621, which is fundamental in the field of optics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Refractive Index**:

 
 
• The refractive index of a substance is a measure of how much the speed of light is reduced inside the substance compared to the speed of light in a vacuum.
 
• It is denoted by the symbol 'n' and is defined as n = c/v, where 'c' is the speed of light in a vacuum and 'v' is the speed of light in the substance.
 
• The refractive index determines how much light is bent, or refracted, when entering a material.
 
• Different materials have different refractive indices, which is why light bends differently when passing through different substances.
 
 
 
• **Snell's Law**:
 
 
• Snell's Law, also known as the law of refraction, is expressed as n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2).
 
• Here, n1 and n2 are the refractive indices of the two media, and θ1 and θ2 are the angles of incidence and refraction, respectively.
 
• This law applies to the refraction of any type of wave, including light, sound, and water waves.
 
• Snell's Law is crucial in designing lenses and other optical devices.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Snell's Law**:
 
 
• Snell's Law is used in various fields such as optics, astronomy, and photography.
 
• It helps in understanding and designing optical instruments like microscopes, telescopes, and cameras.
 
• It is also used in fiber optics for efficient light transmission.
 
• Understanding refraction is essential in disciplines like meteorology and oceanography for studying phenomena like mirages and underwater acoustics.

• The Padma Shri is the fourth highest civilian award in the Republic of India, after the Bharat Ratna, the Padma Vibhushan, and the Padma Bhushan.
 
• Instituted in 1954, it is awarded to citizens of India for their distinguished contributions in various spheres of activity including the arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, medicine, social service, and public affairs.
 
• The award is announced every year on Republic Day, January 26th.
 
• Recipients of the Padma Shri award are announced annually by the Government of India, and the award is conferred by the President of India at a ceremonial function held at Rashtrapati Bhavan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padma Awards**

 
 
• The Padma Awards are one of the highest civilian honors of India announced annually on the eve of Republic Day.
 
• The awards are given in three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri, in descending order of importance.
 
• The Padma Vibhushan is awarded for exceptional and distinguished service, the Padma Bhushan for distinguished service of a high order, and the Padma Shri for distinguished service in any field.
 
• The awards seek to recognize achievements in all fields of activities or disciplines where an element of public service is involved, including the arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, medicine, social service, and public affairs.
 
 
 
• **History and Significance**
 
 
• The Padma Awards were instituted in 1954 to recognize the distinguished contribution of citizens in various fields.
 
• They are a means to honor and celebrate the contributions made by individuals towards the growth and development of the nation.
 
• The awards are a recognition of the hard work and dedication of individuals who have excelled in their respective fields.
 
• They inspire others to strive for excellence and contribute to the nation’s progress.
 
 
 
• **Conferment Process**

• The recommendations for the awards are received from various sources such as state governments, central ministries, previous awardees, and the general public.
 
• The committee reviews the recommendations and submits its recommendations to the Prime Minister and the President of India.
 
• The final list of awardees is announced on the eve of Republic Day, January 26th.

questions.question: Who published Systema Naturae in 1735 classifying the three kingdoms of nature and outlining the sexual system for the classification of plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carolus Linnaeus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Carolus Linnaeus, also known as Carl Linnaeus or Carl von Linné, was a Swedish botanist, zoologist, and physician.
 
• He published the landmark book "Systema Naturae" in 1735, which laid the foundations for the modern biological naming scheme of binomial nomenclature.
 
• Linnaeus classified nature into three kingdoms: animal, vegetable, and mineral, and introduced the sexual system for the classification of plants.
 
• His work in "Systema Naturae" is considered one of the most significant contributions to the field of taxonomy and systematics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Systema Naturae**

 
 
• Systema Naturae is one of the major works of Carl Linnaeus and was first published in 1735.
 
• It introduced a hierarchical classification system, which is the basis for the modern system of taxonomy.
 
• The book included a classification of all known plants, animals, and minerals, and established the use of binomial nomenclature, where each species is given a two-part Latin name (genus and species).
 
• The sexual system of plant classification was based on the number and arrangement of reproductive organs (stamens and pistils).
 
 
 
• **Binomial Nomenclature**
 
 
• Binomial nomenclature is a formal system of naming species of living things by giving each a name composed of two parts, both of which use Latin grammatical forms.
 
• The first part of the name identifies the genus to which the species belongs, and the second part identifies the species within the genus.
 
• This system was developed by Carolus Linnaeus and is used universally in the scientific community.
 
 
 
• **Taxonomy**
 
 
• Taxonomy is the science of defining and naming groups of biological organisms based on shared characteristics.
 
• Organisms are grouped into taxa, which are then grouped into larger taxa, creating a hierarchical structure.
 
• Linnaeus' classification system included ranks such as kingdom, class, order, family, genus, and species, which are still used today.
 
 
 
• **Sexual System**
 
 
• The sexual system was a method of classifying plants based on the number and arrangement of their reproductive organs.
 
• This system was part of Linnaeus' work in "Systema Naturae" and was revolutionary at the time, providing a clear and structured way to classify plants.

questions.question: When a person is NOT paying anything for public goods, it is known as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**free rider**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A free rider is a person who benefits from resources, goods, or services without paying for the cost of the benefit.
 
• This phenomenon commonly occurs with public goods, which are non-excludable and non-rivalrous.
 
• Free rider problem can lead to under-provision of public goods as there is no incentive for individuals to contribute voluntarily.
 
• Government intervention is often required to ensure the provision and maintenance of public goods due to the free rider problem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-excludable:**

 
 
• Non-excludable goods are those that individuals cannot be effectively excluded from using.
 
• Examples include public parks, national defense, and clean air.
 
 
 
• **Rivalrous:**
 
 
• Rivalrous goods are those that can only be used by one person at a time.
 
• If one person consumes a rivalrous good, it reduces the amount available for others.
 
• Examples include food, clothing, and cars.
 
 
 
• **Private good:**
 
 
• Private goods are both excludable and rivalrous.
 
• Owners can prevent others from using them, and their use by one person diminishes their availability to others.
 
• Examples include personal electronics, houses, and personal vehicles.
 
 
 
• **Free rider problem:**
 
 
• This occurs when individuals benefit from resources, goods, or services without paying for them.
 
• It is particularly prevalent with public goods which are non-excludable and non-rivalrous.
 
• Common solutions involve government intervention or collective action to provide the good and ensure everyone contributes.

• The party's manifesto emphasized the need for state socialism in the sphere of industry and agriculture.

questions.question:
With reference of Ajivikas, consider the following statements.

a) Makkhali Gosala was the prominent teacher of this sect.

b) Ajivikas believed in fatalism.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both a and b**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Makkhali Gosala** was indeed the prominent teacher of the Ajivika sect, which is a fundamental point in understanding the history of this ascetic sect.
 
• The Ajivikas were known for their belief in **fatalism**, the idea that all events are predetermined and therefore inevitable.
 
• The sect was a contemporary of Buddhism and Jainism and had a significant influence during the time of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• Ajivikas followed a strict ascetic lifestyle and believed in the concept of niyati (destiny).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ajivikas:**

 
 
• The Ajivikas were an ascetic sect that emerged in ancient India around the same time as Buddhism and Jainism. They believed in the doctrine of predetermination, where every event is preordained and humans are powerless to change their destiny.
 
• **Makkhali Gosala:** He was one of the key figures in the Ajivika sect. His teachings emphasized the power of fate over individual effort.
 
• The teachings of the Ajivikas were based on the principle of niyati, which means destiny. This doctrine suggested that everything in the world was predetermined and fixed, and human efforts to change their fate were futile.
 
• The Ajivikas practiced extreme asceticism and renunciation, similar to other contemporary religious movements like Jainism.
 
 
 
• **Fatalism:**
 
 
• Fatalism is the philosophical doctrine suggesting that all events are predetermined and inevitable, a belief that is central to the Ajivika philosophy.
 
• It implies that human actions have no effect on the future, which is already decided by destiny or fate.
 
• This belief can lead to a deterministic outlook on life, where individuals accept whatever happens without trying to change their circumstances.
 
• In the context of Ajivikas, this meant that their ascetic practices were part of adhering to their predetermined path.

__

• Article 51A (a) of the Indian Constitution lays down the fundamental duty of every citizen to respect the national symbols, including the National Flag.

• **Fundamental Duties**

• The Fundamental Duties are a set of moral obligations enumerated in Part IVA (Article 51A) of the Indian Constitution.

• They were added by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976 upon the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

• Initially, there were ten duties, but an eleventh duty was added by the 86th Amendment in 2002.

• These duties are intended to serve as a constant reminder to every citizen that while enjoying their rights, they have to be conscious of their duties towards the nation.

• The Flag Code of India, 2002, brings together all laws, conventions, practices, and instructions for the display of the National Flag.

questions.question: If sin A - cos A = frac{sqrt{3} - sqrt{2}}{2}, then the value of sin A. cos A is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If sin A − cos A = x, then sin A × cos A = (1 − x²) ÷ 2.

Here, x = (√3 − √2) / 2

⇒ x² = (3 + 2 − 2√6) / 4 = (5 − 2√6) / 4

⇒ 1 − x² = 1 − [(5 − 2√6) / 4] = (2√6 − 1) / 4

⇒ sin A × cos A = [(2√6 − 1) / 4] ÷ 2 = (2√6 − 1) / 8

**∴ The correct answer is (2√6 − 1) / 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sin A − cos A = (√3 − √2) / 2

**Formula Used:**

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

sin² A + cos² A = 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ Squaring both sides of the given equation:

⇒ (sin A − cos A)² = [(√3 − √2) / 2]²

⇒ sin² A + cos² A − 2 × sin A × cos A = (3 + 2 − 2√6) / 4

⇒ 1 − 2 × sin A × cos A = (5 − 2√6) / 4

⇒ 2 × sin A × cos A = 1 − [(5 − 2√6) / 4]

⇒ 2 × sin A × cos A = (4 − 5 + 2√6) / 4

⇒ 2 × sin A × cos A = (2√6 − 1) / 4

⇒ sin A × cos A = (2√6 − 1) / 8

**∴ The correct answer is (2√6 − 1) / 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Trigonometric Identities

sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, sec² θ − tan² θ = 1, and cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1.

Double Angle Formulas

sin(2θ) = 2 × sin θ × cos θ and cos(2θ) = cos² θ − sin² θ.

Sum and Difference Relations

If sin θ + cos θ = p, then squaring gives 1 + 2 × sin θ × cos θ = p², which helps in directly calculating the product of sine and cosine.

questions.question: The least number which must be subtracted from 7278745 so as to obtain a sum that is divisible by 11 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the divisibility rule of 11, find the difference between the sum of alternate digits.

Sum of digits at odd places = 7 + 7 + 7 + 5 = 26

Sum of digits at even places = 2 + 8 + 4 = 14

Difference = 26 − 14 = 12

The remainder when 12 is divided by 11 is 1, so we must subtract 1 from the number.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number = 7278745

Divisor = 11

**Formula Used:**

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let us divide the given number 7278745 by 11 using long division.

⇒ 7278745 = (11 × 661704) + 1

⇒ Quotient = 661704

⇒ Remainder = 1

⇒ To make the number exactly divisible by 11, we must subtract the remainder from the dividend.

⇒ 7278745 − 1 = 7278744 (which is perfectly divisible by 11)

⇒ Thus, the least number to be subtracted is 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places is 0 or a multiple of 11.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the total sum of its digits is exactly divisible by 9.

Divisibility Rule of 7

Double the last digit of the number and subtract it from the remaining truncated part. If the result is divisible by 7, the original number is also divisible by 7.

Remainder Theorem Application

The remainder obtained upon dividing a number is always the least positive value that must be subtracted from the dividend to make it a perfect multiple of the divisor.
</p

questions.question: A motorboat, whose speed in 15 km/h in still water goes 50 km downstream and comes back in a total of 7 hours 30 minutes. The speed of the stream (in km/h) is:

For equal distance upstream and downstream, Total Time = [Distance × (2 × Speed of Boat)] ÷ (Speed of Boat² − Stream Speed²)

⇒ 7.5 = [50 × (2 × 15)] ÷ (15² − s²)

⇒ 7.5 = 1500 ÷ (225 − s²)

⇒ 225 − s² = 200 ⇒ s² = 25

⇒ s = 5 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the motorboat in still water (v) = 15 km/h

Distance covered in each direction (D) = 50 km

Total time taken (T) = 7 hours 30 minutes = 7.5 hours

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Downstream Speed = v + s

Upstream Speed = v − s

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/90d7d394c756d0fc671f442f987c0cb89eb4edd7960a13bb347a629a5b6a8a95.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the stream be s km/h.

⇒ Time taken downstream = 50 ÷ (15 + s)

⇒ Time taken upstream = 50 ÷ (15 − s)

Since the total time is 7.5 hours:

⇒ [50 ÷ (15 + s)] + [50 ÷ (15 − s)] = 7.5

Taking 50 common from the numerator:

⇒ 50 × [1 ÷ (15 + s) + 1 ÷ (15 − s)] = 7.5

⇒ 50 × [(15 − s + 15 + s) ÷ (15 + s)(15 − s)] = 7.5

⇒ 50 × [30 ÷ (225 − s²)] = 7.5

⇒ 1500 ÷ (225 − s²) = 7.5

⇒ 225 − s² = 1500 ÷ 7.5

⇒ 225 − s² = 200

⇒ s² = 225 − 200

⇒ s² = 25

⇒ s = 5 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 5 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Stream

If the downstream speed is D and upstream speed is U, then the speed of the stream = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for Round Trip

When going downstream and returning upstream over the same distance, Average speed = (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).

questions.question: The distance between the longest chord and the centre of a circle is:

The longest chord of any circle is its diameter.

By definition, the diameter always passes exactly through the centre of the circle.

Therefore, the perpendicular distance from the centre to the longest chord is exactly zero.

**∴ The correct answer is 0 unit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Concept Used:**

A chord is a line segment whose endpoints lie on the circumference of the circle.

The length of a chord increases as its perpendicular distance from the centre decreases.

The longest possible chord in any circle is its diameter.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the centre of the given circle be O.

⇒ Let AB be the longest chord of the circle.

⇒ Since AB is the longest chord, it must be the diameter.

⇒ The diameter passes directly through the centre point O.

⇒ The perpendicular distance from a point to a line passing through that same point is zero.

A line segment connecting any two points on the circumference of a circle is called a chord. The perpendicular line drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

Distance and Chord Length Relationship

Chords that are equidistant from the centre are equal in length. As a chord gets closer to the centre, its length increases proportionally.

questions.question: The marked price of 55 items was equal to the cost price of 99 items. The selling price of 56 items was equal to the marked price of 35 items. Calculate the profit or loss percentage from the sale of each item.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Write the given conditions as direct price ratios: MP / CP = 99 / 55 = 9 / 5 and SP / MP = 35 / 56 = 5 / 8

Multiply the ratios to find the direct relation between Selling Price and Cost Price:

(SP / MP) × (MP / CP) = (5 / 8) × (9 / 5) ⇒ SP / CP = 45 / 40 = 9 / 8

Since SP = 9 and CP = 8, Profit = 9 − 8 = 1 unit.

Profit % = (1 ÷ 8) × 100 = 12.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price of 55 items = Cost Price of 99 items

Selling Price of 56 items = Marked Price of 35 items

**Formula Used:**

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/30a3dd5b2504988628f28ca338e1b0ddf382c8570088e57fa30c9f0aa5acb30a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 55 × MP = 99 × CP

⇒ MP / CP = 99 / 55 = 9 / 5

⇒ 56 × SP = 35 × MP

⇒ SP / MP = 35 / 56 = 5 / 8

To equalize the ratio parts of Marked Price, take the LCM of 9 and 8, which is 72.

⇒ MP = 72 units

⇒ CP = (5 / 9) × 72 = 40 units

⇒ SP = (5 / 8) × 72 = 45 units

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 45 − 40 = 5 units

⇒ Profit % = (5 ÷ 40) × 100 = 12.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Formula: Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Discounts

For two successive discounts of x% and y%, the effective single discount is: (x + y − xy / 100)%.

Profit & Loss Relation

Profit or Loss is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise.
</p

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, P received 42% of the valid votes and Q won by 45,360 votes. 20% people did not cast their vote. If 10% of the votes cast were found invalid, what is the total number of votes registered in the poll booth?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the total registered votes be V.

Valid votes = V × 0.80 (cast) × 0.90 (valid) = 0.72V

Q's winning margin = (100% − 42%) − 42% = 16% of valid votes.

Margin = 0.16 × 0.72V = 0.1152V

0.1152V = 45,360 ⇒ V = 3,93,750

**∴ The correct answer is 3,93,750 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Votes not cast = 20%

Invalid votes = 10% of cast votes

P's vote share = 42% of valid votes

Winning margin = 45,360 votes

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a3f97c3db787e3b7297df083b23c643ac85c9b1cf33f59c7a8621791293673dc.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the total number of registered voters be 100x.

⇒ Number of votes cast = 100x − 20% of 100x = 80x

⇒ Valid votes = 80x − 10% of 80x = 72x

⇒ Votes received by P = 42% of 72x = 30.24x

⇒ Votes received by Q = (100% − 42%) = 58% of 72x = 41.76x

⇒ Q's winning margin = 41.76x − 30.24x = 11.52x

⇒ 11.52x = 45,360

⇒ x = 45,360 ÷ 11.52 = 3937.5

⇒ Total registered voters = 100x = 100 × 3937.5 = 3,93,750

**∴ The correct answer is 3,93,750 votes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Valid & Invalid Votes

Invalid votes are calculated only on the total votes cast. Votes not cast are excluded before checking validity.
Formula: Valid Votes = Total Votes Cast − Invalid Votes.

Successive Percentage Change

Election problems often involve successive percentage deductions. The multiplying factor method is fastest.
Formula: Final Value = Base × (1 − a%) × (1 − b%).

Winning Margin

Margin of victory is the difference in votes between the winner and the nearest rival.
Formula: Margin = (Winner % − Loser %) of Valid Votes.
</p

questions.question: Hema is 20 years old and her sister Neha is 30 years old. How many years ago were their ages in the ratio of 3 : 5?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Age difference is always constant. Difference between Hema and Neha = 30 − 20 = 10 years.

The past ratio is 3 : 5. Difference in ratio parts = 5 − 3 = 2 parts.

2 parts = 10 years ⇒ 1 part = 5 years.

Hema's age at that time = 3 × 5 = 15 years.

Years ago = Present age − Past age = 20 − 15 = 5 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Present age of Hema = 20 years

Present age of Neha = 30 years

Ratio of their ages x years ago = 3 : 5

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/71c4be6b761e750403324d70e586ba512dd255c94fdae28f396b1e70c89765eb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the required number of years be x.

⇒ Hema's age x years ago = 20 − x

⇒ Neha's age x years ago = 30 − x

⇒ According to the given ratio condition: (20 − x) / (30 − x) = 3 / 5

⇒ Cross-multiplying the equation:

⇒ 5 × (20 − x) = 3 × (30 − x)

⇒ 100 − 5x = 90 − 3x

⇒ 5x − 3x = 100 − 90

⇒ 2x = 10

⇒ x = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5 years.**

Constant Age Difference

The numerical difference between the ages of two individuals is constant and remains exactly the same throughout their lives.

Time Shifting in Ages

If the current age of a person is P, their age t years ago is expressed as (P − t), and their age t years in the future is expressed as (P + t).

Cross-Multiplication Rule

When solving direct proportions or age ratios of the form a / b = c / d, the most efficient method is cross-multiplication, resulting in a × d = b × c.
</p

questions.question: If cos A + cos²A = 1 then sin²A + sin⁴A is equal to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

From cos A + cos²A = 1, we directly get cos A = 1 − cos²A = sin²A.

Squaring both sides gives cos²A = sin⁴A.

Substitute these into the required expression: sin²A + sin⁴A.

This transforms into cos A + cos²A, which is already given as 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

cos A + cos²A = 1

**Formula Used:**

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

**Calculation:**

⇒ cos A + cos²A = 1

⇒ cos A = 1 − cos²A

⇒ cos A = sin²A

Now, evaluating the required expression:

⇒ sin²A + sin⁴A

⇒ sin²A + (sin²A)²

Substituting sin²A = cos A into the above expression:

⇒ cos A + (cos A)²

⇒ cos A + cos²A

Since it is already given that cos A + cos²A = 1:

⇒ 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

1. sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 ⇒ sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ and cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ.

Secant and Tangent Identity

2. sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 ⇒ sec²θ = 1 + tan²θ.

Cosecant and Cotangent Identity

3. cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1 ⇒ cosec²θ = 1 + cot²θ.

Symmetric Pattern Result

If sin θ + sin²θ = 1, then the symmetric expression evaluates to cos²θ + cos⁴θ = 1.
</p

questions.question: The value of : (1)/(cosec theta - cot theta) - (1)/(sin theta) is equal to:

__Shortcut Trick__

Put θ = 30° in the given expression to solve it directly.

⇒ 1 / (cosec 30° − cot 30°) − 1 / sin 30°

⇒ 1 / (2 − √3) − 2

⇒ Rationalizing the first term: (2 + √3) / (4 − 3) − 2

⇒ 2 + √3 − 2 = √3

Checking the options for θ = 30°, we see that only cot 30° gives √3.

**∴ The correct answer is cot θ.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

1 / (cosec θ − cot θ) − 1 / sin θ

**Formula Used:**

cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1 and 1 / sin θ = cosec θ

**Calculation:**

⇒ Multiply the numerator and denominator of the first term by (cosec θ + cot θ)

⇒ Expression = (cosec θ + cot θ) / (cosec²θ − cot²θ) − cosec θ

⇒ Since cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1, the denominator of the first term becomes 1

⇒ cosec θ + cot θ − cosec θ

⇒ cot θ

**∴ The correct answer is cot θ.**

**__Additional Information__**

Let 1 chair = C and 1 table = T.

10C + 6T = 5140

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum for 8 years is three-fifth of the sum. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Sum be 100 units.

Total Simple Interest for 8 years = 3/5 of 100 = 60 units.

Simple Interest for 1 year = 60 ÷ 8 = 7.5 units.

Rate of interest per annum = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Sum) × 100 = (7.5 ÷ 100) × 100 = 7.5% = 7(1/2)%.

**∴ The correct answer is 7(1/2)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) = 3/5 of Sum (P)

Time (T) = 8 years

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ (3/5)P = (P × R × 8) ÷ 100

⇒ 3/5 = (8 × R) ÷ 100

⇒ 3/5 = 2R ÷ 25

⇒ 2R = (3 × 25) ÷ 5

⇒ 2R = 15

⇒ R = 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5

⇒ Rate of interest = 7.5% = 7(1/2)%

**∴ The correct answer is 7(1/2)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

Interest calculated solely on the initial principal amount. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Compound Interest (CI)

Interest calculated on the initial principal and the accumulated interest of previous periods. Formula: A = P(1 + R/100)T.

Rule of 72

A quick formula used to estimate the number of years required to double the invested money at a given annual fixed interest rate (Years ≈ 72 ÷ R).

SI vs CI Difference

For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI on a certain sum is given by: Difference = P(R/100)².

questions.question: The marked price of a bed sheet is ₹500. At the time of its sale, two successive discounts of 10% and 5% are available. Find the selling price (in ₹) of the bed sheet.

Convert the successive discount percentages directly into multiplying fractions.

5% discount means selling at 95% ⇒ fraction is 19/20.

SP = MP × fraction₁ × fraction₂

SP = 2.5 × 171 = 427.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹427.50.**

questions.question: A mango juice is made by mixing water and mango concentrate in the ratio 9 : 7. If x litres of water and 3x litres of mango concentrate is mixed in 160 litres of mango juice, then the new ratio becomes 13 : 14. What is the quantity of the new mango juice (in litres)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Water = 160 × (9/16) = 90 L, Initial Mango = 160 × (7/16) = 70 L.

After adding x L water and 3x L mango concentrate, the ratio becomes 13 : 14.

⇒ (90 + x) / (70 + 3x) = 13 / 14

⇒ 1260 + 14x = 910 + 39x ⇒ 25x = 350 ⇒ x = 14.

Total new quantity = Initial + Added = 160 + x + 3x = 160 + 4(14) = 216 L.

**∴ The correct answer is 216 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a6f67128abfed30430633093a28bd334805628b9214b505d2d0418771f3cc9f.png] 

**Given:**

Total volume of initial mango juice = 160 litres

Ratio of water to mango concentrate = 9 : 7

**Calculations:**

⇒ Quantity of water initially = (9 / 16) × 160 = 90 litres

⇒ Quantity of mango concentrate initially = (7 / 16) × 160 = 70 litres

After adding x litres of water and 3x litres of mango concentrate:

⇒ New quantity of water = (90 + x) litres

⇒ New quantity of mango concentrate = (70 + 3x) litres

According to the given condition, the new ratio is 13 : 14.

⇒ (90 + x) / (70 + 3x) = 13 / 14

⇒ 14 × (90 + x) = 13 × (70 + 3x)

⇒ 1260 + 14x = 910 + 39x

⇒ 39x − 14x = 1260 − 910

⇒ 25x = 350

⇒ x = 14

Total new quantity of mango juice = Initial quantity + Added quantities

⇒ Total new quantity = 160 + x + 3x = 160 + 4x

⇒ Total new quantity = 160 + 4 × 14

⇒ Total new quantity = 160 + 56 = 216 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 216 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mixtures and Ratios

A ratio compares two quantities by division, written as a:b. In mixture problems, always separate the mixture into individual quantitative parts (like litres) before adding or removing components to find the new ratio.

Cross-Multiplication Method

When equating two fractions to form a proportion like a/b = c/d, cross-multiplication states that a × d = b × c. This fundamental property simplifies equations involving two variables in ratio format.

Addition to Mixtures

If distinct quantities are added to an existing compound, the total capacity increases by the sum of all individual additions. New Total Volume = Old Total Volume + Added W + Added M.

questions.question: Three pipes, P, Q and R, together take four hours to fill a tank. All the three pipes were opened at the same time. After three hours, P was closed, and Q and R filled the remaining tank in two hours. How many hours will P alone take to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Part of the tank filled by P, Q and R in 3 hours = 3/4

Remaining part of the tank = 1 − 3/4 = 1/4

Q and R fill 1/4 part in 2 hours → they can fill the full tank in 8 hours.

Efficiency of P = Total efficiency − Efficiency of (Q + R) = (1/4) − (1/8) = 1/8

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (P + Q + R) to fill the tank together = 4 hours

Time taken by (Q + R) to fill the remaining tank after 3 hours = 2 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work completed by (P + Q + R) in 3 hours = 3/4

⇒ Remaining work = 1 − 3/4 = 1/4

⇒ Time taken by (Q + R) to fill the complete tank = 2 × 4 = 8 hours

⇒ Time taken by P alone = 8 ÷ 1 = 8 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hours.**

Pipes and Cisterns Logic

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours, the part of the tank filled by the pipe in 1 hour is 1/x.

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken. Total Work = Efficiency × Time.

Fractional Work

If a/b part of a work is completed in T days, then the total work will be completed in T × (b/a) days.
